question: In 1959, the Central Government of India undertook the governance in Kerala under _______ of the Constitution of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 356**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1959, the Central Government of India undertook the governance in Kerala under Article 356 of the Constitution of India.**
 
• On July 31, 1959, during Vimochana samaram, Article 356 was utilized for the first time to dissolve Kerala's democratically elected Communist state government.
 
• The States Reorganisation Act of 1956 merged the Malabar district, Travancore-Cochin, and the taluk of Kasargod, South Kanara, to form the state of Kerala on November 1, 1956.
 
• Elections for the new Kerala Legislative Assembly were held in 1957, and E. M. S. Namboodiripad led a reformist, Communist-led government to power.
 
• It was the first time in India's history that a Communist administration was democratically elected to power.
 
• By submitting new measures in the state legislature, it pioneered land reforms and educational reforms. The Catholic Church's opposition in Kerala.
